page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.48xlarge is a top-tier general-purpose cloud compute instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs and 768 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this configuration.

Storage and networking configurations reflect an enterprise network-centric infrastructure model. The server includes no onboard or bundled local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely exclusively on remote block storage or network file systems. To facilitate substantial inter-node data transfers and storage operations, the instance features a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. The substantial bandwidth mitigates potential I/O bottlenecks when communicating with remote disks and peer cluster nodes.

From an efficiency standpoint, the massive 192-vCPU core density allows large organizations to consolidate extensive virtualized workloads onto a single node, lowering hypervisor management overhead. However, achieving cost efficiency requires applications capable of scaling horizontally and vertically across 192 execution threads without thread contention. The lack of integrated disks also means storage performance depends entirely on external network volume allocations.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.48xlarge is best suited for compute-intensive enterprise applications, large-scale backend web serving fleets, distributed memory caching systems, continuous integration pipelines, and high-concurrency relational or transactional database deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.48xlarge is a high-density general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T24 processors at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 768 GB of system memory, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The server includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage architectures supported by a 64 Gbps baseline network connection. From an architectural efficiency perspective, consolidating multiple medium-sized workloads onto this single high-capacity node reduces hypervisor overhead, though workloads must scale effectively across 192 threads to maximize utilization. This instance is well suited for large enterprise container orchestration, high-concurrency relational databases, distributed caching clusters, and high-throughput web serving architectures.
